newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovnaft shares rated buy - Bank Austria.
newsitem.headline: Slovnaft shares rated buy - Bank Austria.

text.p: Shares in Slovakia's sole oil refiner Slovnaft a.s. are rated "buy" despite the company's weak performance so far this year, an investor report issued by the Investmentbank Austria of the Bank Austria Group, said.
"We recommend buying Slovnaft shares... this is a well run company whose management has the ability and the incentive to deliver strong profit growth," the report said.

It did not mention a price for its recommendation. Slovnaft shares closed down 90 crowns at 810 on Thursday and did not trade on Friday, after ranging between 900 and 1,000 crowns level for several past months.

The bank said that despite the company's weak interim performance, it believed Slovnaft would generate a healthy full year result, which will make the shares look cheap relative to regional and international competitors.
Slovnaft posted a pre-tax profit of 1.374 billion crowns for the first nine months of the year, compared with a 3.429 billion gross profit in the same period of 1995.
The company said it would not reach its planned pre-tax profit of around 2.4 billion crowns in 1996.

The report based its recommendation on several further factors, such as the obligation of the majority shareholder in Slovnaft, the management-led company Slovintegra, to provide pre-tax profits of 15.3 billion crowns in the years 1995 to 2001.
"If they fail in this regard, the amount they'll have to pay for (privatisation of their) stake will be much higher," the report said.

Another positive factor is an ambitious investment project designed to reduce heavy oil output from the current 27 percent to about seven percent. The programme is expected to double operating margins when it comes on stream in late 1998.

Investmentbank Austria said it maintained its forecasts of Slovnaft 1996 full year consolidated profit of 1.7 billion crowns, which should be guaranteed by higher-than-expected contributions from the recently recovered market of petrochemicals and plastics.
The report said that Slovnaft had fully repaid its unfavourable long-term loans this summer, which should also result in lower interest expenses in the second half of 1996.
The bank said it forecast Slovnaft's 1997 net profit at 2.0 billion crowns, some 17 percent more than the expected after-tax profit in 1996.
